defaults.permitted_development: A single-storey extension can be permitted development in Wales if it stays within the rear or side limits, remains no higher than 4m, respects boundary controls and uses matching materials.

rules.height_rules: Overall height should not exceed 4m. Eaves should not be higher than the eaves of the existing part of the house they project from. Where any part is within 2m of a boundary, eaves should not exceed 3m.
rules.depth_rules: A single-storey rear extension can project up to 4m beyond the original rear wall. A single-storey side extension should keep the resulting house no more than 50% wider than the original house.
rules.boundary_rules: A single-storey side extension should stay behind the principal elevation and should not be nearer a highway than the existing side wall, or 5m from the highway, whichever is nearer. Any part within 2m of a boundary should not exceed 4m in overall height.
rules.roof_rules: Verandas, raised platforms, roof terraces and projecting balconies are not part of this permitted development route.
rules.materials_rules: External wall and roof materials should match the existing house as closely as practicable.

rules.height_rules: Keep Welsh single-storey work within 4m overall height, do not lift the eaves above the host eaves, and cap eaves at 3m where any part comes within 2m of a boundary.
rules.depth_rules: A single-storey rear extension can project up to 4m beyond the original rear wall. A single-storey side extension should keep the resulting house no more than 50% wider than the original house.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary and highway position are the main side-extension tests in Wales. Keep the work behind the principal elevation, respect the side-wall or 5m highway rule, and control height carefully within 2m of a boundary.
rules.roof_rules: Keep the roof form quiet and subordinate. Prominent front-facing changes, roof terraces and bulky additions are more likely to need express permission in the National Park.
rules.materials_rules: Match the new wall and roof finishes closely to the existing house so the extension reads as part of the dwelling rather than a later add-on.

restrictions.conservation_area: Protected-area controls are tighter in Bannau Brycheiniog National Park. Side and prominent extensions should be checked through the authority before relying on householder rights.
restrictions.listed_building: Do not rely on householder permitted development for a listed building. Bannau Brycheiniog expects listed building proposals to be properly evidenced, and listed building consent will usually be required.

rules.permitted_development: The Welsh single-storey route depends on whether the proposal is rear or side facing, but the recurring tests are 4m height, boundary control, highway position and matching materials.

rules.height_rules: The main Welsh height tests are 4m overall, no eaves above the part of the house extended, and 3m eaves where the extension runs close to the boundary.
rules.depth_rules: A single-storey rear extension can project up to 4m beyond the original rear wall. A single-storey side extension should keep the resulting house no more than 50% wider than the original house.
rules.boundary_rules: If the scheme is side facing, the critical checks are staying behind the principal elevation, keeping clear of the highway test and controlling height where the extension runs close to the boundary.
rules.roof_rules: Keep roof design subordinate and avoid assuming that a roof change attached to the extension is permitted. Prominent roof alterations should be checked through pre-application advice.
rules.materials_rules: Use wall and roof materials that closely relate to the existing house. A modest form with matching finishes is usually easier to defend.

restrictions.conservation_area: Protected-area controls are strong in Eryri. Extensions in conservation areas, and prominent side or front-related work elsewhere in the Park, should be checked formally.
restrictions.listed_building: Listed building consent is required for works affecting the character of a listed building in Eryri, and planning permission may also be needed.

rules.permitted_development: A single-storey extension can be permitted development in Wales if it stays within the rear or side limits, remains no higher than 4m, respects boundary controls and uses matching materials.

rules.height_rules: Overall height should not exceed 4m. Eaves should not be higher than the eaves of the existing part of the house they project from. Where any part is within 2m of a boundary, eaves should not exceed 3m.
rules.depth_rules: A single-storey rear extension can project up to 4m beyond the original rear wall. A single-storey side extension should keep the resulting house no more than 50% wider than the original house.
rules.boundary_rules: A single-storey side extension should stay behind the principal elevation and should not be nearer a highway than the existing side wall, or 5m from the highway, whichever is nearer. Any part within 2m of a boundary should not exceed 4m in overall height.
rules.roof_rules: Do not assume a roof change tied to the extension is covered. In Pembrokeshire Coast National Park, work affecting the roofline is treated more strictly and often needs permission.
rules.materials_rules: External wall and roof materials should match the existing house as closely as practicable.

restrictions.conservation_area: Protected-area controls are tighter in Pembrokeshire Coast National Park. Side elements, prominent extensions and conservation area sites should be checked formally before work starts.
restrictions.listed_building: Do not rely on householder permitted development for a listed building. Pembrokeshire Coast guidance expects listed building consent for alterations or extensions affecting character.
